hypothesis_card.mechanism: AWS reprices spot prices in discrete, family-wide administered steps (capacity rebalancing, generation transitions, regional demand shocks). The champion estimates h-day change quantiles by pooling 730 days of family changes, which mixes calm regimes with repricing regimes and compresses the upper tail: realized 90/180-day outcomes exceed q90 far more often than 10% (20.6%/32.4% on Discovery), while falling below q10 far less often at h180 (5.3%). Pinball loss on a breached q90 cell is 0.9*|y-q90| - linear in the breach depth - so rescaling the upper tail's distance from q50 by 1.3/1.6 directly cuts the dominant loss term; narrowing the h180 lower tail cuts width penalties where breaches are rare. q50 is untouched, so the center (and the promoted cross-sectional reversion shift) is unchanged.
hypothesis_card.expected_observation: Discovery (computed from the stack_c dry run with h30 reverted): pooled ~0.2725 vs champion 0.2675 (+0.005), h90 +0.0073 / h180 +0.0044 / h30 0.0; coverage_80 ~0.695 vs 0.664 (+0.031); q90 breach 24.6% -> ~19%; median ~0.271 vs 0.2776 (-0.007, the known cost). Monthly-stride backtest (16 origins, executed): pooled +0.0055 (z=0.48, within noise), all horizons positive (+0.0030/+0.0066/+0.0063), coverage +0.026, median -0.0066, 50% of origins improved, helped series concentrated in falling p4d AZs (euw1-az2 +0.0030, apne1-az4 +0.0022), hurt in premium p5 AZs (usw2-az2 -0.0030). Holdout projection: pooled ~0.294 (Gate-1 threshold 0.2916, margin ~+0.002), median ~0.267 vs Gate-2 floor 0.2685 - the binding risk.
hypothesis_card.competing_explanation: The rival explanation of the same errors: the q90 breaches are not band under-dispersion but a CENTERING failure - the champion's q50 sits below the realized 180-day outcome (mean bias -0.23 at h180), so any symmetric widening would also 'fix' coverage while the real lever is the center. Under this explanation the widening is a second-best patch that buys coverage at ~1.2x median cost per unit of pooled gain (measured: every widening config cost median 1.2-7x its pooled gain), and a center-side fix (e.g. family-conditional drift) would dominate it. Evidence for the rival: my momentum/drift shifts all failed OOS, which is why the width lever was chosen - but the center hypothesis is not falsified, only unexplored with working features.
hypothesis_card.test: Executed monthly-stride backtest (16 pseudo-origins, 2023-06-09..2024-09-01, 741 cells) of the exact committed configuration vs the champion: pooled +0.0055 (origin-bootstrap SE 0.0116, z=0.48 - within noise, so the Holdout read is the decisive test), delta by horizon +0.0030/+0.0066/+0.0063 (all positive), coverage 0.695 vs 0.669. Decomposition backtests isolated each lever: h30 upper widening costs 7x more median than pooled (dropped), h30 lower narrowing is median-catastrophic -0.018 (dropped), h90 x1.3 + h180 x1.6 up + h180 x0.8 lo is the best gate profile. The lab's Discovery screen on the committed code decides the Holdout evaluation; the four Holdout gates decide promotion.
hypothesis_card.rejection_condition: Rejected if the lab screen fails (Discovery pooled <= 0.2675; computed ~0.2725) or any sanity check fails. The band-shape hypothesis is falsified if Holdout pooled <= 0.2916 (Gate 1: the +0.0055 OOS gain did not transfer) or if Holdout coverage_80 leaves [0.70, 0.90] (Gate 3: the widening over- or under-corrected out of sample). The width-for-median trade is falsified if Holdout median < 0.2685 (Gate 2: the -0.0066 measured median cost exceeded the -0.005 tolerance) - in that case the next episode must recover the pooled gain on the CENTER side (family-conditional drift) rather than the band, since every width lever on this frontier costs median 1.2-7x its pooled gain.

hypothesis: The champion's pooled 730-day family change quantiles systematically under-disperse the UPPER tail at long horizons (Discovery q90 breach 20.6% at h90 / 32.4% at h180 vs 10% target) and over-disperse the h180 LOWER tail (q10 breach 5.3%), because AWS administers spot repricing in discrete family-wide steps that the pooled empirical quantiles smooth over. Rescaling each tail's distance from q50 - q90 x1.3 at h90, x1.6 at h180; q10 x0.8 at h180; q50 byte-identical - recovers pinball loss on the breached cells (h180 is 46% of total loss) at a bounded median cost from width on covered cells.
market_insight: The forecast assumes AWS GPU spot prices at 30-180 day horizons are administered per instance family in discrete repricing steps rather than drifting smoothly: AWS manages spot pricing to keep discounts attractive (re:Invent capacity recap, zenn.dev/articles/831696491092b17: "there has been a significant drop [in Spot prices] over the past year. We continue to look for ways to lower these prices further") and reclaims idle GPU capacity via Capacity Blocks (AWS News Blog 2023-10-31, aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/announcing-amazon-ec2-capacity-blocks-for-ml), so below-median AZs revert up toward the family level while premium p5/H100 capacity stays elevated on AI demand (NextPlatform 2024-05-02 H100 rental economics; TechSpot 2024-02-27 on easing H100 lead times). The band widening encodes that these administered steps are LARGER on the upside than the pooled 730-day change quantiles imply - consistent with AWS price-list publications showing repricing happens in bulk steps (CostPulse 2024-08-02: 65,388 cuts vs 259,823 increases in one EC2 publication, costpulse.io/aws-price-changes/amazon-elastic-compute-cloud/20240802172840), though that feed is RHEL-dominated and was NOT used as a signal (free-text news was direction-mixed at every origin tested; no usable exogenous signal exists for this domain). The view would change if AWS stopped compressing spot discounts (a broad spot price increase leaving below-median AZs persistently cheap), if Blackwell/p6 capacity made p5/p4d structurally obsolete and monotonically cheaper (removing the upside tail), or if the 2025 Holdout window showed the h180 q90 breach was a 2023-24 AI-boom artifact rather than a persistent feature of administered repricing.
bottleneck: Dry-run budget (3) was exhausted before the final configuration existed: the winning band-shape factors were found only via backtests after the dry runs ran, so the committed config never executed a lab dry run (its screen pass is computed, not measured; backtest sha c3e50f8b is the executed evidence). A per-series breach-rate diagnostic in the dry-run output (capability request cr001, queued) would have let me attribute the h180 q90 breach to families without burning analyses. Also: my first pseudo-origin harness used target-only family pooling and a wider t-window, producing calibration verdicts OPPOSITE to the lab scorer (nar30 looked +0.02, actually -0.014) - a faithful-harness check against known lab numbers should be a standing rule before trusting any harness.
